column1: So is India just waiting?
Not at all — and this part might surprise you.
In Visakhapatnam, on a campus of the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, India already runs a rare earth magnet plant.
It's built with our own technology, from Bhabha and a D.R.D.O. lab.
And it makes a special magnet that can take high heat, the kind used in defence and space.
In November twenty twenty-five, the government approved a scheme worth about seven thousand three hundred crore rupees.
The goal?
Six thousand tonnes of magnets a year, made in India.
And the full chain — from rare earth powder, to metal, to alloy, to finished magnet.
Five companies can win up to twelve hundred tonnes each.
This August, twenty bids came in.
Among them, L and T, Coal India and ReNew.
The winners are still to be announced, so keep your eyes on this.
The twenty twenty-six budget also announced special rare earth zones in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Mining, processing, research and factories, all linked up.
And remember the Japan deal?
In June twenty twenty-five, Reuters reported that India asked I.R.E.L. to stop those exports, and keep the rare earths at home.
So the plan is to keep the sand here.
The money is here.
Now comes the hard middle you saw in that chain.
